prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit the attached three-view watercolor turnaround of the chibi light spirit. The user explicitly PREFERS THIS EXACT SWEPT, POINTED HAIR-TUFT HEAD SHAPE and wants its hair tips to fade into translucent light, followed by flame trails and particles.

PRESERVE THE DESIGN: Keep the exact head silhouettes and arrangement of the broad swept pointed tufts in all three existing views. Preserve the full dense lower head volume, face, two small dark oval eyes, tiny mouth, extra-small body, hands, feet, chest core, standing poses, figure scale and positions. Do NOT replace the tufted head with a round bald dome, do not shorten or redesign the tufts, and do not make the whole head transparent. The head's recognizable asymmetrical swept silhouette is essential.

TARGETED CHANGE — A CONTINUOUS ROOT-TO-LIGHT TRANSITION:
1. The lower head and the thick roots / inner approximately 65–75 percent of EACH existing hair tuft stay solid and clearly modeled, with their original pale blue-and-ivory watercolor pattern.
2. In the last approximately 25–35 percent of EACH tuft, gradually reduce its opacity, soften and irregularly dissolve the very edge. Show a little of the neutral paper background through the extreme ends. The transition must be a gentle spatial gradient along each tuft from thick root toward its pointed tip, NOT a hard seam or a uniform haze across the face.
3. Continue a few of the tuft tips into very thin, soft, translucent IVORY-WHITE and PALE-GOLD flame-like light ribbons. They should look like the same material thinning into light, with no visible attachment seam. Follow each tuft's existing backward/upward direction; in the middle RIGHT view these flow toward the upper LEFT. Extensions are short and airy, approximately 10–20 percent of a head width, stay inside each figure's allotted column and do not overlap adjacent views.
4. Add only a handful of small irregular glowing watercolor flecks and a few pinpoints detaching at the far ends, gradually smaller and fainter with distance. Subtle bloom at tips only. Preserve plenty of negative space and a clearly readable original head shape.

The face and body remain sharp and opaque. No fire in front of the eyes, no full-head flame corona, no flames sprouting from the forehead, no orange-red fire, no black smoke, no thick fog, no massive glowing cloud, no human hair strands. Do not add a new anatomical tail, body trail, wings or accessories. This sheet focuses on the gradual transition from the existing sculpted hair tufts into ephemeral light.

Keep the same landscape canvas, neutral watercolor paper background, dashed horizontal alignment guides and the exact labels FRONT, RIGHT, BACK. Exactly three orthographic views with matched scale, no new panels or text. Preserve the hand-painted paper grain and delicate wash boundaries; avoid glossy 3D plastic, photoreal fire or neon.
